client.strengths: Has worked for the same company for 18 years and is highly valued professionally, practically skilled, a loving father, used to be active in the volunteer fire brigade. Keeps to agreements when they are clear.
client.supportNetwork: His wife (supportive but exhausted), his GP, an addiction counsellor at Berner Gesundheit, his line manager, a childhood friend, an AA meeting in Bern (recently).
client.family: Married, two children (13 and 10), lives in Köniz near Bern. His wife works 60% in retail. His father was alcohol-dependent and died at 61. His wife has threatened to separate if nothing changes.
client.education: Trained as a plumber (Sanitärinstallateur EFZ), 18 years with the same installation company, most recently as a service technician with a company van. After smelling of alcohol on a building site and several Monday absences he received a written warning; the company van was temporarily withdrawn.

family.notes: Tension in the marriage, his wife carries almost all responsibility; the children withdraw when he has been drinking. At the same time a strong bond.

schoolWork.notes: Written warning, company van withdrawn; afraid of losing his job. Still valued professionally.

peers.notes: After-work beers with colleagues as a ritual; a childhood friend without an alcohol problem.

health.notes: Raised liver values (GGT), sleep problems, high blood pressure. Outpatient detox with his GP completed without problems.

substanceUse.notes: Increasing use for about eight years, most recently 6–8 glasses of beer (Stange, 3 dl) a day plus spirits at weekends. Morning tremor before detox.

riskBehaviour.notes: Twice drove to work with residual alcohol (not stopped); no driving licence withdrawal.

riskFactors: Stress from overtime and on-call duty (Pikettdienst)

diagnosis.resources: Outpatient addiction counselling at Berner Gesundheit, his GP, counselling for relatives for his wife, AA meetings in Bern; an information meeting at the Klinik Südhang (residential addiction clinic) as an option if outpatient treatment is not enough.
diagnosis.conclusions: Alcohol dependence with consequences for health, work and family. After outpatient detox: a self-chosen three-month abstinence period, followed by a joint reassessment. Involve the employer as far as the client consents; support his wife in her own right.

relapsePlan.lapsePlan: If I drink, I stop after the first glass, tell my wife the same day and call my counsellor the next day. A slip is a signal to adjust the plan – not a reason to give up. If I get withdrawal symptoms, I go to my GP.

client.strengths: Has kept reliably to her opioid agonist treatment for three years, is creative (sews bags), reflective, deeply loves her daughter and has good relationships with addiction services staff.
client.supportNetwork: Her probation officer (Bewährungs- und Vollzugsdienste, BVD – the cantonal probation service), her GP (opioid agonist treatment authorised by the cantonal medical office), a social worker at the Sozialdienst (social services) of the City of Bern, the Kontakt- und Anlaufstelle (K&A – low-threshold contact centre with a supervised consumption room), her mother (a cautious reconciliation), a friend from the sewing workshop.
client.family: Single, one daughter (6) who lives with her father in Burgdorf. Contact every other weekend, currently supervised (arranged by the KESB – child and adult protection authority). Her mother lives in Langenthal; no contact with her brother (32) for years. Her father left the family early on.
client.education: Dropped out of a hairdressing apprenticeship, then worked in catering. Without paid work for four years, supported by social services; works two half-days a week in an employment programme (sewing workshop).

family.notes: A strong bond with her daughter, supervised contact; shame towards her mother, contact being cautiously rebuilt.

schoolWork.notes: No paid work; she attends the employment programme reliably and it gives her a daily structure.

peers.notes: Many contacts from the drug scene; one friend from the sewing workshop who does not use.

leisure.notes: Sewing, walks along the Aare; in the evenings hours of online casino gambling on her phone.

health.notes: Stable on slow-release oral morphine; hepatitis C successfully treated. Lack of sleep after gambling nights, weight loss when using cocaine.

substanceUse.notes: No heroin for three years. Cocaine (snorted, sometimes smoked) once or twice a month, usually after winning or losing at gambling. No additional benzodiazepine use.

riskBehaviour.notes: Online gambling with debts of around CHF 14,000 (consumer loan, health insurance premiums, debt enforcement proceedings). Thefts in the past to finance it.

justice.notes: Suspended prison sentence for repeated theft and fraud; two-year probation period with probation assistance and directives (continuing opioid agonist treatment, debt counselling).

riskFactors: Gambling to regulate emotions and as a supposed way out of debt
Cocaine as a reward or comfort after gambling
protectiveFactors: Her daughter as a strong motivation
Daily structure in the employment programme
A trusting relationship with her probation officer
diagnosis.resources: Probation service (BVD), social services of the City of Bern, Berner Schuldenberatung (debt counselling), the K&A contact centre with a supervised consumption room and basic medical care, a gambling self-exclusion (Spielsperre) via the casinos, gambling counselling at Berner Gesundheit.
diagnosis.conclusions: Stable in opioid agonist treatment, but gambling and episodic cocaine use put her finances, probation and contact with her daughter at risk. Goal: harm reduction (safer use, no cocaine before visiting weekends), self-exclusion and debt restructuring, strengthening her role as a mother. Accompany the directives transparently and without moralising.

goals.achievable: The exclusion applies to all licensed casinos in Switzerland, online too; social services help with the budget.
goals.relevant: Debt is her biggest source of stress.
goals.timeBound: Exclusion within two weeks; monthly review afterwards.

relapsePlan.lapsePlan: If I have gambled or taken cocaine, I talk about it openly at the next appointment. My probation officer has explained what she has to pass on and what she doesn’t. We look at what triggered it, and I keep taking my substitution medication as prescribed. If I mix substances, I am not alone and I have naloxone with me.
